# Turning Innovation
# Into A Heartbeat

We are dedicated to developing cutting-edge fertility tools through continuous research and
innovation. Our advanced tools empower clinics to assist families in realizing their dreams of
parenthood. By integrating the latest scientific advancements, we ensure that our products lead the
way in reproductive medicine. Our commitment to excellence transforms innovative ideas into tangible
solutions. Together, we turn the rhythm of innovation into the heartbeat of new life.

[ About Us ][44]

## IVF Cycle

#### Explore VITROMED’s comprehensive services, designed to support every stage of fertility
#### treatment with precision and care.
* [ Oocyte Collection ][45]
* [ Andrology ][46]
* [ Insemination ][47]
* [ Embryo Culture ][48]
* [ Embryo Transfer ][49]
* [ Vitrification ][50]
* [ Biopsy ][51]

### Oocyte Collection

Oocyte collection is a key procedure in assisted reproductive technologies (ART), designed to
retrieve mature oocytes from the ovaries.

[ Read More ][52]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

### Andrology

Semen sample collection is carried out under strict laboratory protocols, with semen examination and
processing typically following the WHO Laboratory Manual for the Examination and Processing of Human
Semen, 6th Edition (2021). This edition notably highlights semen examination as a sentinel marker of
overall male health, underscoring its importance beyond fertility assessment.

[ Read More ][53]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

### Insemination

Selection of the insemination method—either Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) or conventional
In Vitro Fertilization (cIVF)—is based on semen examination and processing results and the patients’
prior IVF history.

[ Read More ][54]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

### Embryo Culture

Normally fertilized oocytes (zygotes) are cultured under oil for 2–5 days and assessed for quality
either manually or using time-lapse imaging combined with artificial intelligence (AI) to select the
best embryos for transfer.

[ Read More ][55]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

### Embryo Transfer

The selected embryo(s) are transferred into the uterus using a thin, flexible and non-traumatic
catheter, typically guided gently under ultrasound visualization to ensure precise placement in a
simple, non-surgical procedure. Anesthesia is generally not required, though some clinics may offer
mild sedation or pain relief for patient comfort.

[ Read More ][56]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

### Vitrification

Vitrification and slow freezing are the two primary techniques used to cryopreserve embryos and
oocytes in IVF. While both aim to prevent the formation of intracellular ice crystals, vitrification
has emerged as the preferred method in modern clinical practice due to its superior effectiveness in
achieving this goal.

[ Read More ][57]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

### Biopsy

Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) screens embryos for genetic abnormalitiesbefore embryo
transfer and implantation in IVF, aiming to increase healthy pregnancyrates and reduce the risk of
inherited disorders.

[ Read More ][58]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

# Turning Innovation

We are dedicated to developing cutting-edge fertility tools through continuous research and
innovation. Our advanced tools empower clinics to assist families in realizing their dreams of
parenthood. By integrating the latest scientific advancements, we ensure that our products lead the
way in reproductive medicine. Our commitment to excellence transforms innovative ideas into tangible
solutions. Together, we turn the rhythm of innovation into the heartbeat of new life.

### Oocyte Collection

Oocyte collection is a key procedure in assisted reproductive technologies (ART), designed to
retrieve mature oocytes from the ovaries.

[ Read More ][52]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

### Andrology

Semen sample collection is carried out under strict laboratory protocols, with semen examination and
processing typically following the WHO Laboratory Manual for the Examination and Processing of Human
Semen, 6th Edition (2021). This edition notably highlights semen examination as a sentinel marker of
overall male health, underscoring its importance beyond fertility assessment.

[ Read More ][53]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

### Insemination

Selection of the insemination method—either Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) or conventional
In Vitro Fertilization (cIVF)—is based on semen examination and processing results and the patients’
prior IVF history.

[ Read More ][54]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

### Embryo Culture

Normally fertilized oocytes (zygotes) are cultured under oil for 2–5 days and assessed for quality
either manually or using time-lapse imaging combined with artificial intelligence (AI) to select the
best embryos for transfer.

[ Read More ][55]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

### Embryo Transfer

The selected embryo(s) are transferred into the uterus using a thin, flexible and non-traumatic
catheter, typically guided gently under ultrasound visualization to ensure precise placement in a
simple, non-surgical procedure. Anesthesia is generally not required, though some clinics may offer
mild sedation or pain relief for patient comfort.

[ Read More ][56]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

### Vitrification

Vitrification and slow freezing are the two primary techniques used to cryopreserve embryos and
oocytes in IVF. While both aim to prevent the formation of intracellular ice crystals, vitrification
has emerged as the preferred method in modern clinical practice due to its superior effectiveness in
achieving this goal.

[ Read More ][57]

###### Rehabilitation 0

###### User Experience 0

### Biopsy

Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) screens embryos for genetic abnormalitiesbefore embryo
transfer and implantation in IVF, aiming to increase healthy pregnancyrates and reduce the risk of
inherited disorders.

[ Read More ][58]
